title: How is everyone doing 3D clothing fitting without clipping?
author: Cheedows
selftext:
Been struggling with this for the past week, trying to find a way to have my clothing in a 3D game layer properly and be fitted to my characters and races without any clipping. Going to be honest it's been a struggle, even with models with 3D capabilities like Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5. Thinking there's surely something I'm missing and it's a solved problem but regardless of method or algorithm it all turns out to be a mess.

Especially with things like cloaks or coats, or skirts and dresses, anything that extends past the torso and it's a disaster. Wondering if anyone else has had much luck getting this to work and what's your workflow?

comments.author: Cry_Havoc_1990
comments.body:
I think the problem is trying to use AI to actually do this work.

For this kind of adjustments, it might be better to ask Claude the steps involved in setting up physics for clothes or how to prevent clipping, but you may actually have to do the work. 

What I have to do is write me up a written guide and tell me everything in blender that I need to do because it cant see it, but it knows what to do. I don’t remember any blender, hot keys, etc. so this is my workaround.

comments.author: Ok_Feedback4200
comments.body:
Research how clothing is made in 3D. Also, attach images if you want help with your exact clippings. No idea what kind of models you are working on.

When you work with a character and clothing in 3D, you start with a character in A-Pose. Then simulate your clothing on top of that pose so you have it as nice static model that's fitted to A-Pose.

In games, clothing should have a combination of both skinning to the body and dynamics to get the cloth moving. For animations, you'd do a full simulation of clothing inside a software like Marvelous Designer or similar. That would give you the best quality 3D clothing possible but each simulation has to be recalculated based on your animations and it gets very slow. For games, if you want a trully great quality, you should create your clothing in a similar manner to how it's done inside Marvelous Designer too just skip the full simulation and instead build a system inside your game engine which will drive the cloth dynamics...

comments.author: Ok-Forever7812
comments.body:
The only workarounds I've had success with is shortening any flowing bits, minimising areas that use or need cloth physics, or doing it myself unfortunately.  AI will eventually be better at this but for now I'm not sure there's a good solution.  If you absolutely must use the AI to do this today and absolutely need cloth physics on them, you'll need to get creative and potentially look to older or retro style games featuring skirts, cloaks etc for inspiration on workarounds or a good enough solution.    
  
Skirts and cloaks have been in games long before modern cloth simulation was widespread.  We just had to get creative with them.  The AI might even be able to help mock up some alternative ways to get there through animation

comments.body:

comments.author: R_dva
comments.body: you need to ask experienced 3d artist how to do it

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: So I had to deal with this in my 2D game due to the amount of items underneath layers and the fact that no matter how hard I tried I would still have some items that clip through others. My solution was literally just having Claude build an anti clip mechanism where if an article of clothing / equipment extends past a certain point on another item essentially becomes invisible. Claude simply does not allow clipping in these instances. It was simple in a 2D game but it’s essentially a micro layer erasing surrounding an object unless the object far exceeds the layer then it fully ignores the object. I can see a 3D version of this working.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: Have you considered actually buying a solution from the asset store? There are many very refined solutions for this available.

comments.author: Mrbuttshaman
comments.body: I had no idea how to do a lot of this stuff about a month ago.  I asked Claude how to do a lot of these things.  One thing I asked was how to handle this, and well... I'll give you a secret.  You can just ask it to write something that does it for you using existing commercially viable free libraries and then ask it to make it so it can interface with it directly as needed.  It will absolutely take care of everything itself.  This applies to literally everything you can possibly do through software.  With enough trial and error it will figure out what you want, and create a workflow for you to achieve it with almost no involvement once you set it up.
